decisions.reason: Because conferencing is close to the firm's managed communications base and can be supported with existing network, platform and service capabilities, management is likely to keep it despite only limited early evidence.
This product fits the firm's core data-centre and metro-network strengths and already shows concrete customer adoption, so absorptive capacity and market relevance both support keeping it.

Optical spectrum connectivity builds directly on the firm's fibre assets and engineering knowledge and matches its move toward high-bandwidth software-defined infrastructure, making withdrawal unlikely.
A voice number ordering portal extends existing voice and provisioning know-how and supports the firm's push toward real-time digital service operations, so it is likely to be retained.

Although it is close to the firm's established voice business, carrier pre-selection is a more legacy-style telephony offer and is therefore the most exposed to pruning in a declining market, but existing capabilities still make retention slightly more likely than exit.

Direct voice network connection remains adjacent to the firm's enterprise communications offer and can be serviced with current infrastructure and support teams, so management would usually keep it while monitoring demand.
